data.title: Secondary Payload / Additional Tool Installation
data.summary: Beyond fetching a single second-stage payload, the sample installs one or more additional, separately-functioning programs — a different malware family, a legitimate but unwanted tool, or a persistence helper.
data.description:
This is distinguished from simple ingress tool transfer by intent: rather than retrieving
its own next stage, the sample is acting as an installer or loader-for-hire, bringing in
entirely separate software with its own independent capability and lifecycle. This pattern
is common in pay-per-install criminal ecosystems, where an initial infection vector is
monetised by installing whatever a buyer has paid to have distributed.
data.recommendation:
* Inventory every additional program installed, not only the initial sample — each may be a distinct family requiring its own independent analysis and remediation.
* Treat the installing sample as a loader-for-hire indicator; its presence does not bound the actual threat to what it alone does.
* Check installation timestamps against the initial infection window to establish whether additional installs happened immediately or were staged for later.
data.short_recommendation: Inventory every additional program installed independently; each may be a distinct family needing its own remediation.

mitre_techniques.procedure: Downloaded and silently installed a separate, independently functioning program via a bundled installer after initial execution.

mbc_techniques.implementation: Installed a separate program with its own independent persistence and capability, distinct from the initial payload.
